newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips still in talks with Grundig family.
newsitem.headline: Philips still in talks with Grundig family.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday it was still in talks with the Grundig family and the Max Grundig Foundation about further disentangling links with the company.

Loss-making German consumer electronics company Grundig has weighed heavily on Philips' earnings in the past. At the beginning of 1997 Philips stopped consolidating 100 percent of Grundig's losses, accounting only for its 31.6 percent stake.
"As far as discussions with the Stiftung (foundation) and the family are concerned, they continue," vice chairman Dudley Eustace said after announcing a rise in first quarter profits.
Eustace said discussions were moving slowly but the talks were making progress.

"I would hope that we (will) have much more positive and definitive news when we sit down here for the second quarter review. There's not an awful lot I can say while we're in discussions with them but there's an ongoing dialogue," Eustace told a results news conference.
Grundig has yet to report any figures for 1997 but last year made a net loss of 553 million marks.
Eustace declined to quantify the extent to which Grundig's removal from the operating line had helped the consumer product unit return to profit, saying only the impact was significant.
"Grundig's out, that in itself makes for a significantly better picture," said Eustace.
Philips wants to dissolve the pact with the Max Grundig Foundation under which it pays 45 million marks a year to the Grundig family heirs, passive majority shareholders in Grundig.
The pact, which gave Philips control of the firm despite its minority stake, would also have Philips buy the 68 percent of Grundig it does not already own in 2004 for 540 million marks.
